facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old woman
31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder
depressed mood, anhedonia, nervousness, fatigue, decreased appetite, and poor sleep
beginning 5 months after COVID-19
two severe episodes responsive to escitalopram (up to 20 mg/d) and duloxetine (up to 60 mg/d)
intolerance to venlafaxine, bupropion, and trazodone
mother had mania
denied iron deficiency anemia, hypothyroidism, or substance abuse
Physical and neurologic examinations and routine laboratory tests were unremarkable
new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms
worse at rest, partially relieved by movement, and predominantly occurring in the evening
causing night-time sleep disturbance

concepts.why: The patient has a 31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder and is experiencing depressed mood, anhedonia, nervousness, fatigue, decreased appetite, and poor sleep.
The patient developed new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms after increasing duloxetine, which is a known side effect of the medication.
The patient has a history of recurrent depressive disorder and has not responded to multiple treatments, including escitalopram, duloxetine, venlafaxine, bupropion, and trazodone.
The patient developed depressive symptoms 5 months after COVID-19, which may be related to the infection.
The patient experienced night-time sleep disturbance after increasing duloxetine, which is a known side effect of the medication.
The patient has a family history of mania and a personal history of recurrent depressive disorder, suggesting a possible genetic component to her mood disorder.
The patient developed paresthesias after increasing duloxetine, which may be related to medication-induced neuropathy.
The patient is experiencing anhedonia, which is a key symptom of depression.
The patient is experiencing fatigue, which is a common symptom of depression.
The patient is experiencing poor sleep and night-time sleep disturbance, which are common symptoms of depression.

rationales.F02: The patient's 31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder supports the diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder and Treatment-Resistant Depression.
rationales.F03: The patient's symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia, nervousness, fatigue, decreased appetite, and poor sleep are characteristic of Major Depressive Disorder and Depression with Anhedonia and Fatigue.
rationales.F04: The onset of symptoms 5 months after COVID-19 supports the diagnosis of COVID-19-associated Depression.
rationales.F05: The patient's response to escitalopram and duloxetine suggests that they have had some benefit from treatment, but the fact that they have had two severe episodes and are currently experiencing symptoms despite treatment suggests that they have Treatment-Resistant Depression.
rationales.F07: The patient's family history of mania supports the diagnosis of Familial Mood Disorder.
rationales.F10: The patient's new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms are characteristic of Duloxetine-induced Paresthesia and Medication-Induced Neuropathy.
rationales.F12: The patient's night-time sleep disturbance is characteristic of Depression with Sleep Disturbance and Duloxetine-induced Sleep Disturbance.
